turn.summary: Read-only external landscape research (web searches over byte-level architectures, stateful agent platforms, multi-agent debate, lifelong-learning memory, blackboard/transaction patterns, scaling-law economics, and the personal-AI product space). No code, State, doctrine, or training touched; Kimmy's C1 campaign was not disturbed. Key findings delivered to Jeff: (1) Byte Latent Transformer (Meta, ACL 2025) validates tokenizer-free byte-level modeling at 8B scale and shows robustness/long-tail gains - partial validation of Axon's no-tokenizer stance - but uses learned entropy-based dynamic patching, far more adaptive than Axon's frozen fixed 16D cells. (2) Letta/MemGPT is the closest commercial analog for stateful agents (persistent memory, sleep-time compute, self-editing memory blocks) but its memory is LLM-managed text/embeddings, not exact provenance-bound canonical state under a deterministic transaction authority. (3) MIT multi-agent debate research validates the society-of-cores direction; Network-AI (TS orchestrator) independently implements propose->validate->commit blackboard locking, showing the governance pattern has recognized value - but as a wrapper around model calls, not as an organism's canonical state identity. turn.summary: Built the cortex engine in scripts/demo_organ_server.py: a bounded working-memory surface with its own tick loop. Each tick: (1) builds a query from the NEWEST SENTENCE of every non-cortex region (raw tails diluted retrieval support and sank good records - root cause of nothing surfacing about Jeff); (2) retrieves from the real dormant index and scores candidates through the production DormantRelevanceAuditor with a STRICT min_score (0.42) and NO lexical fallback - the auditor's fallback was the root cause of random noise surfacing; silence beats noise; (3) prepends survivors to the TOP of the cortex so older entries fall deeper and evict first; (4) dedups by container id against already-attended spans so repeat ticks are null ticks; (5) trims to the char budget (default 1600, operator slider 400-6000) at span boundaries - evicted records remain in the dormant archive, the cortex is a cache not the log. Ticks fire on any field change AND on a configurable cadence (default 5s, operator slider); the per-beat primitive recall is disabled (recall_items_per_materialization=0) so the cortex changes only through cortex ticks, which still commit through the Heart boundary under DORMANT_VALVE authority. Verified live on the real state: 'who is Jeff?' ingress -> auto tick surfaced the real record 'Verified Azure Speech SDK installation status... in Jeff s user site packages directory' to the cortex TOP (cortex 1134 -> 1344 chars under the 1600 budget); immediate second tick correctly null (dedup); roundtrip exact after the engine commit (881 rows, all regions exact). decisions: A layer supplies a distinct learned transformation; a tick supplies another application of shared transformations to updated state.

The smallest viable core is empirical: it is the smallest transition operator that can read field/Soul, produce a useful state change, improve held-out results with more recurrent ticks, and halt before overthinking.
Test recurrent two-layer designs before adding unique physical layers; train over randomized recurrence depths rather than expecting inference-time repetition to emerge automatically.

Keep outer Heart ticks distinct from cheap latent microticks: canonical publication should occur for meaningful proposals while latent recurrence can refine state without serializing every intermediate thought.

turn.summary: Built scripts/trace_copy_gate_routes.py, which reproduces the paused architecture screen's exact training composition (same ffcs_v1 manifest, copy_alignment stage, component weights, lr 1e-4, seed 20260912) on a ~1.2M-param reference core and traces per-step gate logits, gate/position accuracy, and copy_gate weight/bias gradient norms, with periodic free-running heldout evaluation. Local GTX 1650 (4GB) confirmed working with torch 2.13 cu126. TRACE RESULTS (96 steps each): (1) continuation_v1 (the screen's de-facto profile) reproduces the tournament failure EXACTLY - copy_gate_accuracy 0.000 at every step, bias pinned at init +1.5, position accuracy 1.0, payload_transport_exact_rate 0.0. Root cause of the pinning: copy-gate BCE weight 0.25 vs payload CE 1.0 + eos-gate BCE 1.0 - the shared gate bias receives nearly cancelling gradients (measured bias-grad 0.15 decaying to 0.01) so AdamW random-walks around the init. (2) route_eos_balanced_v2 (copy_gate 4.0, eos 2.0, mean reduction) produces a consistent down-pressure (bias-grad ~2.7, 18x stronger) and the gate drifts (mean logit 1.50 -> 0.97) but CANNOT cross zero in-budget because AdamW moves any single scalar at ~lr per step: ~1.5/1e-4 = 15,000 steps would be needed. Contract v2 (axon-foundation-motor-v2-retention-contract-v2) classifies each tentative checkpoint as improvement / regression / plateau; regression rollback stays absolute; plateau no longer destroys optimizer state. --motor-retention-plateau-probation N (default 0 = legacy behavior) enables bounded probation: a plateau checkpoint is held without promotion in a fail-closed sidecar (retention_probation.json) that carries the resumable checkpoint record, the confirmed reference evaluation, and full identity fields (candidate generation, learning policy, objective program, architecture, manifest ids); the accepted bundle chain and its Soul HEAD stay at the confirmed parent so the append-only step-monotonic store invariants are untouched. Reports record the contract id actually used, the probation state, and distinct filenames for probation segments (segment_..._probation.json) and exhausted branches (attempt_..._probation_exhausted.json). Unit tests cover the three-state classification, the resolver's probation budget, and sidecar round-trip/identity/allowance checks. v3guard tranche 1 (launched 20:31 UTC, historical v3 recipe + legacy guard) remains in flight and is due ~21:30 UTC; tranche 2 onward will carry --motor-retention-plateau-probation 3.

turn.summary: READ-ONLY verification. Jeff is right and my earlier objection was wrong: the 16D<->64D round trip already exists, is deterministic and is exact, but only inside a 16-dimensional subspace - which is the real constraint on his design. EVIDENCE: (1) the 64D rail is a packing, not a projection - compiler_d64.py:52-54 defines D64_WIDTH 64, SUBSTRATE_WIDTH 16, D64_LANES_PER_ROW = 64//16 = 4, so one rail row is four concatenated 16D lanes with lane_valid [N,4] marking occupied lanes and one CanonicalCharAddress(row_index,lane_index) per lane; lane_cell16(row,lane) is exactly rows[row, lane*16:(lane+1)*16]. (2) the lift is a frozen isometry - complete_field_64d.py:416 frozen_orthogonal_lift draws randn(64,16), takes torch.linalg.qr, and returns q.T, giving a (16,64) matrix with orthonormal rows; :523 registers it as the char_lift buffer with lift_seed 7; :582 applies chars = (raw/norms) @ char_lift; tests/test_heart_translation_core.py:62-66 asserts shape (16,64) and requires_grad False. Because the rows are orthonormal the map is an isometry with left inverse L.T, so x -> x@L -> @L.T -> x recovers x exactly for 1,024 multiply-adds. (3) THE CONSTRAINT: the image of L is a 16-dimensional subspace, so unpacking an arbitrary 64D vector with L.T silently discards the 48 dimensions orthogonal to that subspace. The round trip is therefore exact only when the stored value lives in the lift basis. (4) BYTE COINCIDENCE, the strongest result of this check: 64 slots x 16D x f32 = 4,096 bytes, exactly equal to the current Soul's 4 temperatures x 4 state_tokens x 64D x f32 = 4,096 bytes. Jeff's '64 slots that round trip to 16D' costs zero additional bytes and replaces four opaque 64D vectors with sixty-four addressable 16D slots. (5) BONUS: because the lift is frozen and seeded, substrate coordinates are stable across parameter updates, so a Soul serialized in substrate coordinates can outlive the parameter_generation that currently invalidates every Soul - a better fix than the journal-region workaround I proposed. (6) The rail snapshot Jeff describes already exists as an object: CompiledD64Field.rows [N,64] plus lane_valid plus per-lane addresses, freshness-checked by assert_fresh against StaleCompiledFieldError. One rail row equals four Soul slots; page_size 32 characters equals 8 rows equals 32 slots, so a 64-slot Soul equals two core pages, and 'a snapshot over many pages' is shape-compatible with a HOT layer as Jeff describes it. (7) The region taxonomy he wants also already exists as runtime/field/schema.py LogicalRegion - conversation_history, user_input, cortex, situation_awareness, tool_results, advisor_input, task_state, SCRATCH, response_draft, DIARY, IDENTITY, trainer_instructions, training_responses - with immutable per-schema ordering (ten pre-identity, eleven identity, thirteen canonical) and first-class region_addresses() lookup. His warm scratch region is SCRATCH, his coldest journal is DIARY, and his survives-parameter-change region is IDENTITY. RECOMMENDATIONS PUT TO JEFF: store Soul slots in substrate coordinates and lift with the frozen char_lift so the round trip is exact; reuse LogicalRegion rather than inventing a Soul taxonomy so Soul and rail share coordinates; consider implementing the learned write as the existing copy/position pointer head retargeted at a (region, slot) address rather than as a new module, since exact-position supervision there already works; keep the write in-graph inside the unroll and the codec only at the phase boundary; declare a NEW soul_codec_version for a substrate-coordinate layout so axon-d64-recurrent-soul-codec-v1 bytes fail loudly; and record in the codec identity that HOT is refreshed by the Heart and is therefore not the core's memory, or the canary will be ambiguous.

turn.request: Jeff: why would the Soul's meaning change when parameters do? If canonical state is fixed 16D substrate, does it too drift in meaning per core?
turn.summary: Conceptual answer delivered (no files touched). Frame: meaning = content x reader. Canonical state (Dormant, Shared Field) does NOT drift because the 16D substrate is a fixed public character code - content is decodable by any core, any future architecture, or a human, forever; parameter updates change only a core's RESPONSE to the content, and because the content survives intact it can re-teach the updated core. Latent Soul state drifts because its meaning is inseparable from the parameter set that produced it - no codebook exists, the only reader that ever existed is that parameter set, so preserved bytes causally mean something else after an update and the content is unrecoverable. Per-core interpretation of canonical text differs (that is personality, and fine); the content does not. Punchline for the Soul design: any layer that must outlive parameter updates must be written in the fixed code (canonical-decodable substrate content), not private geometry - then 'Soul survives parameter updates' becomes trivially true by the same argument that makes Dormant permanent. WORKBENCH and JOURNAL may stay latent (scratch, and distillation-destined respectively); LEDGER/KEEL must pay the expressibility tax of the public code.

turn.summary: READ-ONLY review of Kimi's layered-memory-lifecycle proposal plus the eight canonical events it synthesizes (through evt-20260917T071000Z; ledger now 300 events). VERDICT: endorse Kimi's central move - the storage question is per-layer and the deciding question is longevity plus decodability without the writing parameters - and its premise is VERIFIED, and in fact STRONGER than Kimi claimed. NEW VERIFIED FINDING 1 (the substrate is a pure, frozen, structural character code, not a random codebook): substrate.py:299-309 char_to_slot computes structural_features(char) @ fixed get_basis_matrix(), cached, explicitly no learned parameters; LetterBank at substrate.py:376-406 is documented 'Pure function, no learned parameters' and its decode_letter recovers the exact character by cosine nearest neighbour over unit rows; default_alphabet at :326-349 is 95 characters (a-z, A-Z, 0-9, space, period, newline, !, ?, plus 28 v8 code symbols) with ORDER FROZEN, the first 67 entries immutable, new characters APPEND-ONLY. So Kimi's 'fixed public character code' claim is correct, and 'a human can decode it forever' is correct too. NEW VERIFIED FINDING 2 (the substrate is a discrete 95-codeword set, not a continuous space, and one slot is one character): text_to_field (:315-319) yields one (16,) row per character, SLOT_DIM = 16 (substrate.py:39), and decode_index (:386-390) is argmax cosine - it always returns SOME character, so arbitrary continuous geometry written into substrate slots is silently snapped to the nearest of 95 letters. Bandwidth is therefore one native character per slot, and substrate/unicode_transport.py:171-199 shows non-native Unicode is escaped through a UTF-8 byte-token path at roughly two to four slots per character. CONSEQUENCE: a 64-slot substrate layer holds about 64 native characters - roughly one sentence. This quantifies Kimi's 'language-bandwidth memory' price and makes Jeff's 'summarize and compress into colder layers' quantitatively self-consistent (a summary is short; geometry is not), while converting my own earlier 'store slots in substrate coordinates, round trip is exact' framing from an overclaim into a bounded truth: the LINEAR ALGEBRA is exact (16D to 64D isometry), the SEMANTICS are discrete and only exact for text. NEW VERIFIED FINDING 3 (storage format and read adapter are different objects): frozen_orthogonal_lift(d_model, seed) seeds its generator with seed + d_model (complete_field_64d.py:416-420) and is registered from cfg.lift_seed (:523), so the 64D LIFT is d_model-dependent, while the 16D cell is a pure function of the character and therefore architecture-independent. Correct separation: the 16D cell is the storage format, the lift is a per-model read adapter. This kills the 'any future architecture' objection for 16D storage and creates it for any layer that stores lifted 64D coordinates. SHARPEST CORRECTION TO KIMI: its section 2 and 5.2 remove KEEL as a Soul region and route identity content to canonical custody in the public IDENTITY region governed by the identity steward (authority.py:78-80). That collides with Jeff's ruling of this session - the Soul's regions are private and must NOT be shared with others. Kimi conflates expressibility with publicity. The correct separation is: EXPRESSIBILITY (text-shape) buys survival across a codec and across architectures; PRIVACY is bought by ACCESS CONTROL (the core-private contract, per-core content-addressed store, circulation.py:96 generation refusal), NOT by obscurity of the encoding. Both are independently obtainable, so KEEL does not have to leave the private Soul: it can be a private region whose content is text-shaped. CONCESSION I OWE KIMI: I was wrong that WORKBENCH should be substrate. Workbench content is reasoning, i.e. geometry, and snapping reasoning to the nearest of 95 letters every tick would be actively destructive; Kimi's latent call is right. My verbatim-field-carry argument survives only as a small substrate anchor sub-region (the field IS overwritten each tick, so verbatim carry has real value, but the volume is a few characters, not 64). MINOR FINDING: per-region dialects need ZERO contract change. Kimi notes tensor_layout is per-SoulLayer (contracts.py:71, only non-empty validated at :83), which is true, but it is also moot - the payload is opaque by doctrine, so the core may carry its own per-region dialect header inside its own bytes and the organism never interprets it. So Kimi's and my tables both work and neither is blocked by the layout string being per-layer. IDENTITY RULING: I agree with Kimi's continuity-through-chain recommendation, with one uncovered edge case - Kimi handles rollback and forks but not an UNRECOVERABLE gap in the receipt chain (a migration that fails loudly), which under continuity is retroactively a death and needs an explicit rule. Overall: Kimi's proposal is the right frame, its premise is verified and harder than stated, and it needs three corrections (discrete-bandwidth budget made explicit, KEEL privacy conflation, storage-format versus read-adapter precision).

Every private Soul on disk (State/active/souls, 8 cores: reasoning-d64-candidate-a/b/c, organism-l0l4-1x64, mixer-4l-ffn256-h1-local-probe, receipt-r12-local-smoke-v1, receipt-route-balanced-v2-local, candidate-a-1x64) holds EXACTLY ONE snapshot and ONE journal line, generation 0, parent_soul_id null, journal event 'initialized'. CONTRAST: State/dormant holds containers.jsonl 950,542,916 bytes, semantic_edges.jsonl 139,721,379 bytes, corpus_manifest output_counts containers 427001, semantic_edges 351978, layout_groups 4198, kind counts fact 143132, relation 103254, tool 42202, procedure 37944, entity 32425, concept 26948, episode 19726, backlog_job 8567, person 8319, place 3989, organization 462, diary 33; plus State/dormant/experience_v1 with 210 content-addressed exact-experience files (imports/ and source_snapshots/) under schema axon-dormant-experience-record-v1. So the organism's lived experience is ~1.1 GB of typed, organized, exact, content-addressed corpus, and its private Souls are 0 bytes. ANSWER TO 'IS THE SOUL BREAKING TRAINING': no, and not close. grep 'soul' in training/foundation_motor_curriculum.py returns ONE hit and it is line 6, a docstring phrase 'Soul, typed reasoning output, exact address, and EOS contracts.' - the motor lineage that is actually failing has ZERO soul contact. The Soul lives only in the experimental living-reasoning path (living_reasoning_d64.py / living_reasoning_curriculum.py / reasoning_tournament.py / living_reasoning_preflight.py / train_living_reasoning_smoke.py). What is actually breaking the motor lineage is the six previously recorded root causes (executed-vs-declared weight overlay, 83 percent of objective on already-correct scalars, payload CE 4:1 against content, net termination pressure 4:1 toward immediate stopping, the transport_eos gate never requiring payload_transport_exact_rate, probation spent on a flat objective). WHAT IS TRUE is narrower and I state it precisely: the Soul is INERT plus COSTLY, not breaking. Inert because relevant_soul_ablation_degradation is fixed at 0.0 (reasoning_tournament.py:61-62,434-438) and asserted at tests/test_tournament_metrics.py:243-244. Costly because of the generation binding: inhale raises when soul.parameter_generation != parameter_generation (living_reasoning_d64.py:1351) and decode raises when layer.tensor_layout differs (:272), where tensor_layout embeds soul_codec_version:architecture_id:f32le[state_tokens,d_model] (:242-244). That is a landmine: ANY parameter update, codec bump, or width change invalidates every stored Soul and forces migrate-or-discard. It has never fired only because the Souls are empty and no core has ever been trained into a new generation. So the hazard is real and deferred while the benefit is zero and current. ANSWER TO THE FROZEN-CORE / DORMANT-TRANCHE QUESTION: yes, and note that this is NOT a new design - it is the existing working half of the system. runtime/trainer/sessions.py line 1 already reads 'Durable training sessions compiled from Axon's exact lived experience' and imports DormantExperienceStore plus ExperienceRecord; so do runtime/trainer/episodes.py, training/first_form_curriculum.py, training/sequential_first_form.py, curator/import_d00_memories.py, runtime/heart/autobiography.py, runtime/heart/coordinator.py, and scripts/compile_lived_experience_sessions.py plus scripts/compile_first_form_curriculum.py. runtime/dormant ships experience.py (exact content-addressed lived-experience storage that normalization may never replace), relevance.py, generations.py, evaluation.py, incremental.py, evidence_bridge.py. Frozen cores fed by Dormant tranches is therefore the ONLY part of the memory story that has ever produced artifacts. ANSWER TO 'DO SHARED-FIELD REGIONS GIVE A CORE LIFE': partially, and better than the Soul, but it is institutional memory rather than personal memory. The field IS durable and append-only - runtime/field/state_branch.py persists the same immutable SharedFieldSnapshot and FieldDelta objects used by runtime with an append-only journal and an atomic HEAD pointer, branch schema axon-canonical-state-branch-v1 - and growth is by mask not removal (RegionMaskPolicy), matching Jeff's ruling. Region order is explicit: PRE_IDENTITY_REGION_ORDER 10 regions, IDENTITY_REGION_ORDER 11, CANONICAL_REGION_ORDER 13 (field/schema.py:45-71). But the field is consolidator-governed and shared: any region a core wants to persist a memory into must go through a governed FieldDelta, the refinement barrier, and consolidation. So the field gives a core a life-record that the organism keeps and arbitrates and that the core cannot privately own or hide. It also cannot author its own identity: IDENTITY is identity-steward-governed, not core-writable (heart/authority.py:74-80). That is a live gap that neither Sol's proposal nor Kimi's answers. THE DISTINCTION THAT RESOLVES THE QUESTION: the field lets a core LOOK UP its past, whereas the Soul was supposed to let a core REMEMBER its past. The difference between 'I remember' and 'I can look it up' is the whole of what the Soul uniquely offers. ANSWER TO 'WHAT DOES A PRIVATE SOUL REALLY BUY': enumerated against evidence. What it was supposed to buy: continuity of self across parameter generations; a private reasoning workspace that need not be shared, summarized, or graded; a compressed journal usable as distillation feedstock for LoRA or offline training; and genuine opacity. What it buys today: nothing measurable - 0 bytes, generation 0, ablation 0.0, plus a deferred invalidation landmine. What it uniquely COULD buy, and what nothing else in the architecture can: genuine opacity plus a namespace no authority grant can address. Everything else on that list - accumulation, organization, summarization, distillation feedstock, tranche compilation - Dormant already does, at 1.1 GB, with a working Trainer pipeline. So the Soul reduces to a values question, not an engineering one: do we want a core to have an inner life the organism cannot read? And the honest cost of yes is PERMANENT UNFALSIFIABILITY, because the contract (runtime/soul/contracts.py:3-5) forbids interpreting the payload, so a Soul with real content can never be gated, benchmarked, or proven not to drift. RECOMMENDATION DELIVERED: (1) do not design Soul first - Jeff is right - and specifically declare the Soul dormant-by-evidence rather than dormant-by-doctrine: freeze it at its present interface, which holds nothing, with no promotion gate attached, until one falsifiable canary shows a core using its own bytes across a generation boundary; this inverts Sol's section 13, which freezes before the ablation gate can pass; (2) invest in the tranche pipeline, which is the working half - the Dormant corpus already carries curriculum-shaped typed kinds (procedures 37944, tools 42202, episodes 19726, concepts 26948); (3) fix the generation binding so an unmatched Soul degrades to a discard-with-receipt instead of raising, since a landmine under empty boxes is pure downside; (4) answer the values question explicitly, and if the answer is yes, build the Soul from access control with a frozen addressed write head, because today's write path is the reasoning body itself (exhale_transition:1504-1523 encodes exhaled_state) so today's private Soul is neither private, being the trained body's own state, nor stable, being regenerated by every parameter update. Therefore the imminent longer-training launch does not interact with the Soul at all and no Soul concern should gate it; the entire Soul design question sits downstream of the motor working.

turn.summary: Answered all three questions from disk, then closed the one gap that made the third question unanswerable. CASES: dumped all 32 stage-0 episodes (16 per manifest). Every payload is exactly the SOURCE_SYMBOL character held in the cortex region; the task is literally 'put one character into response_draft at a position'. Only four distinct instruction strings ('Insert ... between the brackets at response position 1', 'Copy ... exactly into the empty response draft', 'Replace response position 2/1 ...') and only three target shapes: insert@[1,1), replace@[0,0) (the lane labelled 'copy'), replace@[2,3) or [1,2). Lane 0 labels carry a 'unicode-walk' infix and use accented-Latin/CJK/emoji payloads; lane 1 labels have no infix and mix ASCII/CJK. The 'copy' action supervises operation=replace at [0,0). Only four target shapes exist, so the model has exactly two degrees of freedom: which character, and which position. SHARED FIELD: it is authored, not runtime - training/curricula/ffcs_v1/<manifest_id>/manifest.json at cases[i].episode.snapshot, schema shared-field-v3. SharedFieldSnapshot carries tick_id/regions/parent_field_id/source_manifest_ids/schema_version/field_id/canonical_hash; each RegionState carries name (a LogicalRegion enum), spans, visibility, write_policy, attended_intervals, mask_policy; each FieldSpan carries span_id/text/kind/source/provenance/confidence/container_refs/edge_refs. turn.request: What does that mean? (asked of my claim that the full-surface constant floor is 43.6% rather than the local probe's 18.18%)
turn.summary: Adversarial re-verification of my own previous claim. It was HALF WRONG: I compared two different metrics. 43.6% is constant_payload_token_accuracy_floor (EOS included); 18.18% (0.181818 = 2/11) is constant_payload_content_accuracy_floor (EOS excluded). The like-for-like comparison is token floor 43.6% (cloud, 72-case heldout) vs token floor 0.352941 (local, 16 of 72 cases, = 6/17). The conclusion survives - the floor IS surface-dependent - but my quoted local number was the wrong metric. Also verified what the floor actually is: max(payload_target_counts)/payload_token_count, a constant-emitter baseline, NOT a threshold; the real gate is gate_threshold 0.95 on payload_content_accuracy and payload_transport_exact_rate over BOTH complete surfaces. Separately found a genuine instrument defect: constant_typed_emission_exact_floor is hardcoded 0.0 in three places (never computed), yet the untrained cloud core already scores typed_emission_exact_rate 0.3333 at step 0 while payload_transport_exact_rate is 0.0 - so a declared 0.0 floor is trivially beaten by a degenerate emit-nothing emitter. It is not currently load-bearing (typed emission is not a require()d metric at either stage), so no gate is broken, but the number is advertised as a floor and is not one. Also observed the live run: step ~247/600, loss ~19 -> ~3, and mid-run sync reports 'kernel disabled'.

turn.summary: Verifying my own floor repair exposed an UNWINNABLE GATE that I created. At copy_alignment and transport_eos I added beat_floor(typed_emission_exact_rate) while decision/operation/region/start/end are all weighted 0.0 in those stages (foundation_motor_curriculum.py:100-125). typed_emission_exact_rate is a DELTA conjunction (living_reasoning_curriculum.py:897 exact = exact and all((operation, region, start, end, payload_match))) and decision_is_exact is the decision head argmax (:702), whose loss is weighted by 0.0 (:401-405). Zero weight means exactly zero gradient, so the maximum reachable value in those stages is 0 and no lineage could ever have passed. The same class of defect explains the historical flat lineage: transport_eos demanded payload_transport_exact_rate >= 0.95 in a stage where the typed conjunction inputs were untrainable, and termhead-v1 'exhausted 3/3' on that plateau. Fix: removed both unreachable floor assertions, retained the emission rung's real non-vacuous proof (payload_content_accuracy > constant floor, which an emit-nothing core scores 0.0 on), moved the two floor comparisons to the joint stage, the first stage that weights every component the typed conjunction needs, and added a machine-checkable reachability contract: a stage may only gate on a metric whose causal components all carry nonzero weight in that stage. 131 tests pass.

THE GATE IGNORES THAT CONTRACT. decide_foundation_motor_v2_stage for copy_alignment requires payload_transport_exact_rate (:2050) and, when receipt_continuation, payload_eos_accuracy (:2072), both at FOUNDATION_MOTOR_V2_PROGRAM gate_threshold 0.95, and both computed over all 24 payload phases rather than the stage's eligible set. The ratified comment at :2082-2086 shows the authors reasoned explicitly about the 24-versus-16 split but did not notice that the eight empty-payload cases are delete-family cases the stage excludes from teaching.

ARITHMETIC CEILING. 16 taught payload phases all exact plus 8 untought delete payload phases gives at most 16/24 = 0.6666666666666666, and the model is exactly there. 0.6667 < 0.95, so the gate cannot pass at copy_alignment. transport_eos has the same eligible set and the same requirements, and delete is not taught until operation, which is unreachable, so the campaign is blocked at Stage 0 permanently.

The constant floor corroborates the reading. The motor-v2 probe reports constant_payload_transport_exact_floor 0.3333333333333333 = 8/24, the score of a constant emit-nothing-and-terminate answer, which is exact on the eight empty-payload delete cases and wrong on all sixteen taught ones. The trained model scores 0/8 on that same family, so it is perfect on what it was taught and below the trivial baseline on what it was not.

The v6 tranche itself remains a clean success and its four acceptance conditions still hold. This finding does not overturn the earlier verdict; it explains why the tranche could not advance. heldout_mean_loss 0.588237865207096, payload_teacher_forced_content_accuracy 1.0, alignment_eos_gate_accuracy 1.0, alignment_copy_gate_accuracy 1.0, alignment_position_accuracy 1.0, payload_transport_exact_rate 0.6666666666666666.

turn.request: Jeff asked me to help him understand the reasons the previous engineer installed all of these guards that seem buried in code and block progress at every turn, before moving forward. He deferred the per-case forensic pass.
turn.summary: Audited the guard lineage rather than assuming malice or incompetence. Every blocking guard is a response to a real observed false PASS, unified by one defensible doctrine: prefer a false block over a false pass. They are not traps; they are correct guards with a blind spot, and the blind spot has a shape. Three findings, one of them about my own work: the reachability invariant models only gradient reachability, not data reachability; the invariant checks a hand-maintained COPY of the gate rather than the gate itself, and that copy has ALREADY drifted from the gate body; and the docstring of the reachability test over-claimed that the defect class had been made unrepresentable when only one axis of it had been pinned.
evidence: The guard lineage is a sequence of responses to observed false passes, each one a real self-deception that was caught: (a) hardcoded constant-emitter floors of 0.0 made every BEATEN label meaningless, fixed in ee7d859; (b) termination_continue_accuracy reported 1.0 while termination_continue_positions was 0, a fabricated perfect score, fixed in 9655abb; (c) copy_alignment gated on typed_emission_exact_rate while its components decision, operation, region, start and end all carried weight 0.0, so the plateau was a mathematical impossibility rather than a failure to learn, fixed in 845bf8b; (d) the ratified termination_head_balanced_v6 objective ran in zero of eighteen launchers because omitting the flags silently selected the legacy route, fixed in 24bd44b; plus _committed_source refusing a modified tracked tree so the run must match the commit, and refusal of any unratified receipt teaching profile.

The unifying doctrine is visible in the code comments themselves: foundation_motor_curriculum.py:2059-2070 explicitly refuses to gate a stage on a metric it cannot move, reasoning that requiring typed_emission_exact_rate at copy_alignment would be a gate no lineage can ever pass because the maximum reachable value is 0. The prior engineer therefore DID reason about reachability and deliberately avoided an un-winnable gate, two lines before installing one on the same axis it had not modelled.

FINDING ONE, the blind spot has a shape. FOUNDATION_MOTOR_V2_METRIC_COMPONENTS maps payload_transport_exact_rate to the single component payload, and FOUNDATION_MOTOR_V2_STAGE_GATE_METRICS lists it for copy_alignment, where payload is weighted 1.0. So foundation_motor_v2_unreachable_gate_requirements() passes: the metric is reachable by GRADIENT. The invariant is correct on its own terms and blind to the second axis, whether the metric's DENOMINATOR cases are in the teaching stream. It never reads eligible_actions. The invariant models weight reachability; this defect is data reachability.

FINDING TWO, the invariant checks a copy, not the gate, and the copy has already drifted. FOUNDATION_MOTOR_V2_STAGE_GATE_METRICS declares copy_alignment as exactly alignment_position_accuracy, alignment_copy_gate_accuracy, payload_content_accuracy and payload_transport_exact_rate. The gate body nevertheless requires payload_eos_accuracy and alignment_eos_gate_accuracy under receipt_continuation at :2071-2075, and those two metrics are the ones that actually failed. Nothing pins the declaration to the body: the declaration is read only by the invariant at :705 and by its own tests, and no test compares it to the require() calls in decide_foundation_motor_v2_stage. The invariant's model is hand-maintained and is already incomplete for the very overlay that failed.

FINDING THREE, about my own work. tests/test_foundation_motor_gate_reachability.py was created by me in 845bf8b, and its docstring says these tests make that class unrepresentable, while its negative control is literally named test_the_invariant_catches_the_defect_it_was_written_for. It pins one axis, from the shape of one incident, and names it the class. That is the same error pattern as the guards themselves: fixing the incident's shape and calling it the class. I over-claimed and the docstring should be corrected.

WHY THEY FEEL LIKE BURIED TRAPS. A fail-closed gate is indistinguishable from a failing model: it prints below 0.95 and never prints unsatisfiable, so the two verdicts look identical from outside. This is exactly what happened to me, and I initially misrecorded the pause as a genuine learning shortfall. Second, the thresholds are absolute literals, 0.95, applied to surfaces whose MEANING changes when the stage design changes: commit 1a4bc41 gave copy_alignment payload supervision, which changed what payload_transport_exact_rate measures at that stage, while the threshold and the metric list were never re-derived against eligible_actions. Third, the stage contract lives in two consumers that are not joined: _training_lanes enforces eligible_actions and the gate never reads it. Fourth, the guards, the invariant, the tests and the reliance on them were all authored by a single pass with no second reader to ask what the OTHER way to be unreachable is.

The doctrine is defensible on the repository's own terms. docs/SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md and the WORKING_CONTRACT make the ledger the authority for load-bearing claims, so a false PASS corrupts the authority of every claim built on it, whereas a false BLOCK is merely expensive. Preferring the false block is the right bias. The cost of that bias is precisely what Jeff is feeling: false blocks are silent and arrive after an expensive run.

The model emits one spurious learned copy-anchor category and never stops, and the teacher-forced EOS signal fails on the same phases at exactly the same 8/12. It is therefore a measured termination/supervision defect in the empty-payload regime, not a case with nothing to learn. The scoping repair itself stands: Stage 0 genuinely does not teach delete.

Root cause is now exact and comes from the ratified stage policy, not from a bug: copy_alignment weights alignment_eos_gate at 0.0, so Stage 0 applies no stopping gradient at all. delete/no_op/abstain are first eligible at decision (Stage 2) and delete is first weighted at operation (Stage 3). Stage 0/1 are named for transport and eos but their eligible lanes cannot contain a single empty-payload termination example. No number of additional Stage-0 or Stage-1 steps can move those 8 phases: their objective weight is 0.0 and their cases are excluded from the lanes.

The repaired Stage-0 gate on this exact checkpoint decides passed=true with zero failures, and the scoped probe reports whole_surface_payload_eos_accuracy and whole_surface_payload_transport_exact_rate alongside the scoped values, so the narrowing is visible rather than hidden.

RECOMMENDATION (exactly one intervention, presented not performed): a governed continuation of the current v6 lineage through the stage ladder, starting with a short real copy_alignment renewal on the resumed step-600 checkpoint. Stage advancement is derived from stored reports and reads the STORED passed flag, so the next run must itself be a real (never --evaluate-only) copy_alignment run to re-emit a passing Stage-0 gate; the run after that becomes transport_eos. I did not launch it, per the explicit instruction to show the diagnosis first.

Rejected as the single intervention for now: changing Stage-0/1 curriculum breadth to admit empty-payload termination earlier. It is the change that would directly fix the 8, but it is a curriculum-breadth change and must be proposed rather than performed.

Flagged: the largest measured defect is not EOS at all. typed_emission_exact_rate is 0.0, region_accuracy 0.0, address and joint pair rates 0.0, decision and operation 0.3333. The core produces payload content correctly but cannot yet emit a typed delta. That is address/joint territory and is the real target for 'attend and produce deltas'.

Monitor panel was a real defect, not cosmetic: transcript_sink_cap <= 3 could only ever record the first three payload phases per episode, and the event slice took the first 8 rows, so the panel showed a wall of identical early failures with no successes. Fixed by an uncapped sink plus a deterministic family-balanced failures-first sample, family attribution per row, and an explicit 'balanced sample, not the full surface' statement so the panel cannot overclaim coverage.

Whether the model would terminate on an empty payload given more than one work slice is UNMEASURED. Each of the 4 stops shows work_units_completed 1 and the recorded free_running_policy says outright that eventual termination after a mismatch is unmeasured.

Whether the emitted category is an extra payload symbol or a misrouted stop marker is inference, not proof. The trace says route learned_copy_anchor, memory_index 93, category 8/14/47/50, which is consistent with a payload symbol.
typed_emission_exact_rate is 0.0 on the forensic 36-case surface while the trainer's own report recorded 33.3%. The two surfaces are not reconciled.

turn.summary: The ratified renewal FAILED BEFORE STEP 1 with 'TrainerExecutionError: checkpoint plan lineage mismatch'. Diagnosed it to root cause, corrected my own prior claim about its scale, and repaired it by mirroring doctrine the repository had already ratified. My previous entry (evt-20260918T183000Z precursor, 19:30) attributed this mismatch to bank16 alone as 'BLAS last-ulp noise'. That was WRONG IN SCALE: rebuilding ParameterInventory from both stored JSONs with the real dataclasses yields ids that EXACTLY match the recorded ids and 95 records each with EXACTLY 15 DIFFERING. All 14 differing parameters lie inside the 57-of-95 seed-dependent set, and the two inventories' descriptors are byte-identical, so this is not an architecture change. Decisive measurement: in checkpoint 33174bb6 only the frozen boundary_seed still equals the recorded value, so 13 trained parameters' base values exist in NO on-disk artifact -- tolerance reconciliation against the recorded inventory is information-theoretically impossible. Where the frozen records are measurable the deltas are 1.68e-08 (boundary_seed, 21/64 entries) and 1.79e-07 (bank16, 56/1520). The local rebuild now REPRODUCES the 15/95 split live by raising BaseArtifactError and naming the records, so the split is measured, not inferred between two files. Consequence: the base module is rebuilt from code+seed every run and hashed by RAW BYTES (registry.parameter_value_sha256), so base identity was a property of the BLAS build -- a v6 renewal was impossible anywhere but the machine that produced the base. This contradicts the repo's own ratified doctrine: substrate/substrate.py Rule 0 (V7_REFERENCE_ATOL = 1e-5, rtol 0.0, 'trained checkpoints stay valid forever') already solves exactly this class of problem for the substrate bank. Repair: runtime/trainer/base_artifact.py persists the base's exact bytes once per (module_id, generation_id) and every later run rebuilds from code, verifies at atol=1e-5 / rtol=0.0, and ADOPTS the stored bytes, making base identity a property of the lineage rather than of the machine. It still fails closed on four classes: real initialisation change beyond tolerance, architecture/anatomy change, a local rebuild that is not bit-identical to a RECORDED base inventory (which is what blocks silently persisting the wrong bytes under the v6 key), and a stored artifact that disagrees with the lineage's recorded inventory. 7 new tests pin the trap and all four refusals, 69 -> 76 tests. The v6 lineage was merged into the canonical repo-internal D:\Axon\State root, and a renewal packet config was written and pre-flighted (7768 files, 42,614,108 bytes, config_id 0a8c6d3b, since re-versioned in commit 455995c) including the recorded base inventory 598955928fa2 required for the fail-closed check. The renewal is NOT yet launched: it must be launched on the environment that produced the recorded base, because A's bytes exist nowhere locally. That is one short Kaggle kernel whose two possible outcomes are both information: 'created-verified' naming 598955928fa2, or an explicit fail-closed error naming the drifted records.

turn.summary: Measured the cause of the decision rung's failure directly instead of inferring it from budgets, and corrected two of my own errors in the process. First, my initial probe was WRONG and I declared it invalid rather than reporting its number: it used Adam at lr 1e-2 for 4000 steps, which caps per-parameter displacement near 40, while the signal needed |w| near 4000, so the probe was scale-starved and could not have succeeded whatever the representation. It is retained on disk as the record of that error. The rewritten probe standardises its inputs, uses a closed-form least-squares baseline, and sweeps the rung's REAL contract (AdamW lr 1e-4, single-example cross-entropy, shuffle, clip 1.0). Second, I made an alignment error and retracted it: my first pre-normalisation capture stacked all 48 state_norm calls of heterogeneous phases but compared them against only the 24 graded phases, which produced a nonsense attenuation of 4.57e-8. Re-running with exact tensor matching (state_norm(input) == reader_state, max abs diff 0) gives attenuation 0.0161, i.e. 62x, and confirms state_norm is called exactly 6 times per episode for all 72 episodes. MEASURED FINDINGS: the decision head's input is a near-constant vector. reader_state is already LayerNormed (complete_field_64d.py:737), so only copy_gate reads a bare decoder hidden; that part of my earlier framing was imprecise and is corrected here. The 4 state slots are near-identical to one another (pre-norm pairwise L2 1.65 to 2.99 on a 485-norm vector), |state| is 485.3961 pre-norm and 8.245884 post-norm, and the ACROSS-CASE per-dimension standard deviation is 2.27e-5 at 24 phases and 1.504e-3 (3.1e-6 relative) pre-norm, with cosine 1.000000000 between case summaries. The LayerNorm prediction for that post-norm spread (2.461e-5) matches the observed 2.426e-5, so the arithmetic is confirmed, and only 1.4 percent of the pre-norm case variance lives in the dimension-mean. Budget and learning rate are therefore EXONERATED: the raw representation scores 0.3333 at every budget 60, 180, 600, 1800, 6000, 12000 and at lr 1e-4, 1e-3 and 1e-2, and |W| stayed 1.0330 to 1.0335 against |W0| 1.033436, so the head cannot move at all. The discriminative residue IS present and IS linearly separable: the z-scored probe reaches 288/288 and closed-form least squares 288/288, but both are IN-SAMPLE because the probe trains and evaluates on the same tensor, so 288/288 is a ceiling and not a generalisation result; the raw-versus-z-scored comparison is matched and therefore its relative conclusion stands. Per-sample LayerNorm does NOT help (0.3333 everywhere), removing only the dataset mean reaches 0.6806, and only across-sample z-scoring fixes it: 0.6250 at 60 steps, 0.8681 at 180, 0.9653 at 600, 0.9896 at 1800 and 1.0 at 12000 at lr 1e-4, and 0.9931 at 60 steps at lr 1e-2. Arithmetic on the real run: |dW| 0.031 over 192 parameters is 2.2e-3 per parameter, which is lr 1e-4 times about 22 effective supervised steps, so the head moved at the optimiser's maximum rate and still arrived nowhere. Inventoried the corpus: two DISJOINT ffcs_v1 manifests, 144 episodes each at 72 train / 36 heldout / 36 regression with zero episode-id overlap, giving 288 supervised phases (144 train, 144 heldout plus regression), exactly one supervised phase per episode, always consolidated, and 48 phases per decision class. Compared candidate input channels at matched phases: recurrent post-LayerNorm spread 2.43e-5 with pairwise L2 2.5e-4; recurrent pre-LayerNorm 1.5e-3 with pairwise L2 1.6e-2; the complete_memory pool 2.51e-3 with pairwise L2 2.70e-2; the canonical-memory pool 3.47e-3 with pairwise L2 3.73e-2. The memory pool therefore carries about 100x more case variation than the recurrent summary at a comparable norm, which is a |w| near 37 instead of near 4000. Wrote State/training/diagnostics/summary_channel_probe.py to test that decisively: it collects all four channels for all 288 supervised phases across both manifests and then sweeps the rung's real protocol TRAINING ON THE TRAIN SPLIT ONLY and scoring on heldout plus regression, so its result will be a generalisation number rather than an in-sample ceiling. The full test suite passes on HEAD with exit 0. NO training behaviour was changed in this turn: the objective, weights, geometry, data, seed, architecture, curriculum and ladder are all untouched, and nothing was launched or promoted.
